## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9156. ⭐ The round corrected FOUR things, and one of them retires a rule this seat has been applying all shift

Reviewed against the diff, ⛔ not the report. Every reading below is this seat's own.

### ⛔ Correction 1 — my ⛔ said this gate runs in `docs-route-eager-closure.yml`. It does NOT, and the line I matched says so.

That workflow's only `run:` for the job is `pnpm check:docs-route-closure` — `scripts/check-docs-route-eager-closure.mjs`, a **different gate**. My `git grep -ln check-eager-closure-budget -- .github/workflows` hit **two comment lines**, and the first of them reads:

> `# The gate `check:eager-closure` is not (objectui#6316).`

⇒ ⭐ **the disconfirming evidence was inside the very line my grep returned.** This is errata 43 — 「**containment is not authorship**」 — for the **third** time this shift, and errata 38's shape on top of it. ⛔ A file that NAMES a script is not a file that RUNS it, and a `grep -l` cannot tell the difference.

Only `performance-budget.yml` references it, and only in a **paths filter**.

### ⛔ Correction 2 — ⭐ and this one retires a standing rule

My claim said 「neither is among the **nine** required merge-queue contexts」. The dev measured `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`: `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` holds **26** entries and `Docs Route Eager Closure Check` **is** one; `Bundle Analysis` sits in `OPTIONAL_CONTEXTS`.

⚠️ ⭐ **But the deeper reading is worse for me, and it is in that file's own header:**

> The gate does NOT ask GitHub 「are the required checks green?」 — that question is answered by the **branch-protection required set**, which is a repository-SETTINGS surface this repository can **neither read nor change** … and which is **demonstrably not carrying the shards today: a merge occurred while all four were `in_progress`, so none of them can be in it.**

⇒ ⛔ **my 「nine required contexts」 is not the required set.** It is the nine I observed going green before every merge — and this repo has **measured** that the shards are not in the branch-protection set at all. ⚠️ I have been calling that list 「required」 in every dispatch order and every ACCEPT this shift. ⭐ The list is still a useful substantive checklist; the word 「required」 was never derived.

⇒ this seat's errata-40 rule is amended: **check the gate list against the repo's own `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` (26, derived and tested), and say 「the contexts CI reports」 rather than 「required」 unless the branch-protection set has actually been read** — which from inside this repository it cannot be.

### ⭐ Correction 3 — the conclusion survives, on a BETTER reason than either of us gave

Verified: `merge_group` appears in `performance-budget.yml` **only inside a comment**, recording that 300 sampled runs contain zero `merge_group` runs. `ci.yml` **does** subscribe `merge_group`.

⇒ Bundle Analysis **cannot hold the merge queue at all**, whatever the ruleset says about pull requests — and `scripts/**/*.test.ts` runs in the shards, which **do** run on `merge_group`. ⭐ So the floor belongs exactly where it was put, ⛔ but 「because the shards are required」 was the wrong reason; 「because the shards RUN on `merge_group` and Bundle Analysis does not」 is the right one.

### ⛔ Correction 4 — 「107 tests」 was 107 CALL SITES

`grep -cE '^\s*(it|test)\('` → **107**; `it.each`/`test.each` → **6** more call sites, which **expand**. ⇒ 113 call sites, **127** cases. The dev's numbers reconcile with mine exactly; my error was labelling call sites 「tests」.
⭐ Errata 46's family again: **a count is a population only if the pattern selects the population you mean.** I have now made that mistake twice in three cards.

### ⭐ What the fix actually is, and why the shape is right

```js
if (unrecognised.length > 0) return { code: 2, unrecognised };
const statuses = entries.map(([, status]) => status);
if (statuses.includes('error')) return { code: 2, unrecognised };
return { code: statuses.includes('fail') ? 1 : 0, unrecognised };
```

⭐ **The two precedence tests survive byte-identically** — `statuses.includes('error')` and `statuses.includes('fail') ? 1 : 0` are the same expressions as on the base. ⇒ the 「error outranks fail」 ordering objectui#5490 established is **relocated, ⛔ not re-derived**, which is the one thing the fence protected.

⭐ And the unrecognised test sits **ahead** of the `error` test on purpose, with the reasoning in the file: both return 2, so order cannot change an exit code — **what it changes is whether the caller is told**. ⛔ A sibling half erroring in the same run must not absorb the one signal that a status nobody enumerated exists.

⭐ **The rejection of 「a default that throws」 is decided by measurement, not taste:** `node -e 'throw'` exits **1**, which is this file's 「over budget — a real verdict about the bundle」 code. ⇒ a throw would report a broken gauge **as a size regression** — the exact collapse `main`'s own comment refuses. 「Louder」 in words, mislabelled in the only unit a workflow reads.

### The six new cases, and the two that make them non-vacuous

- LOUD about an undeclared status · names the offending half **even when a sibling errors** · ⭐ **keeps `not-applicable` inert in the very run an unrecognised status is loud** — the control of known direction, and it is the whole card in one run.
- ⭐ **「recognises exactly the statuses this file declares, re-derived from its source」** — the tripwire for the fifth status.
- ⭐ **「extracts statuses at all — a matcher that matches nothing agrees with everything」** — the non-vacuity control **for that re-derivation**. ⛔ Without it a source-grepping test passes when the grep matches nothing.
- ⭐ **「is the fold `main` itself uses, not a parallel copy」** — guards against testing a duplicate.

| the precedence pair | **byte-identical expressions** |

| a fifth status anywhere | **none** |
| `Bundle Analysis` on this PR | **success** — it does run, per its paths filter naming this very file |
| `Docs Route Eager Closure Check` | **success** |
| reds | **NONE** |

⚠️ ⭐ And the round filed **objectui#9155** bare: six prose sites call `Bundle Analysis` a required context, against the classifier beside them and against the no-`merge_group` measurement. ⇒ that is AGENTS.md #9's class exactly — a 「verified」 claim with nothing re-deriving it — and it is the same defect my own claim carried.

⇒ **ACCEPT**, pending the remaining contexts. Flipping to ready once they converge; the Armed note with the probe goes up **before** the merge.

## Armed — `SQUASH`, merge queue entered. ⭐ Probe written HERE, ⛔ before the merge

`added_to_merge_queue` confirmed. Head `e7b2f5aa1`; **34 checks, 0 red, 0 pending**; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` **success post-flip**.

⚠️ ⭐ **This note does NOT say 「required contexts」.** Per the retraction in the ACCEPT: that set is a branch-protection surface this repository cannot read, and its own classifier records that a merge occurred with all four shards `in_progress`. ⇒ what is stated below is **what CI reported**, ⛔ not what is required.

Every expected value was read off `e7b2f5aa1` — ⛔ none from the report. ⭐ The census hash was reproduced independently here and matches the dev's.

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git fetch origin main -q
G=scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs
T=scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts

echo "── LANDED, per file ──"
printf '%-48s %s\n' 'RECOGNISED_HALF_STATUSES entries (expect 4)' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$G | awk '/RECOGNISED_HALF_STATUSES = /,/\]\);/' | grep -cE "^\s*'")"
printf '%-48s %s\n' 'foldHalfStatuses occurrences (floor 3)' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$G | grep -c foldHalfStatuses)"

echo "── SURVIVED — the precedence pair, RELOCATED not re-derived ──"
printf '%-48s %s\n' 'statuses.includes( occurrences (expect 2)' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$G | grep -c 'statuses.includes(')"
git show origin/main:$G | grep -nE "statuses\.includes\('(error|fail)'\)"
# both lines must fall INSIDE foldHalfStatuses, and NONE inside main
awk '/^export function foldHalfStatuses/,/^}/' <(git show origin/main:$G) | grep -c 'statuses.includes('   # expect 2

echo "── SURVIVED — the status census: HASH paired with a COUNT ──"
git show origin/main:$G | grep -oE "status: '[a-z-]+'," | sort | uniq -c
printf '%-48s %s\n' 'census sha256 first16 (expect 45bfa910d7644f01)' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$G | grep -oE "status: '[a-z-]+'," | sort | uniq -c | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"
printf '%-48s %s\n' 'total status literals (expect 21)' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$G | grep -cE "status: '[a-z-]+',")"

echo "── LANDED — the cases, FROM THE RUNNER ──"
pnpm exec vitest run "$T" 2>&1 | grep -E '^\s*Tests '     # floor: 138 passed

echo "── SCOPE: the merge commit's own diff ──"
git diff --name-only <MERGE_SHA>^ <MERGE_SHA>              # expect exactly the gate and its test
```

### Expected, and where each comes from

| leg | expect | read from |
|---|--:|---|
| `RECOGNISED_HALF_STATUSES` | **4** — `pass` `fail` `error` `not-applicable` | the frozen list on the head |
| `foldHalfStatuses` occurrences | floor **3** (landed 5) | a **floor**, ⛔ not equality — prose may legitimately name it again |
| `statuses.includes(` | **2**, ⭐ **both inside `foldHalfStatuses`, none inside `main`** | the base had exactly 2, in `main` |
| the census | **14** error · **2** fail · **1** not-applicable · **4** pass | ⭐ hash `45bfa910d7644f01` **paired with** total **21** |
| cases | floor **138** | ⭐ **from `vitest run`**, ⛔ not from a grep |

⭐ **Why the precedence leg is shaped that way.** A bare count of `statuses.includes(` would read **2** on the base too — the fix **relocated** those two expressions rather than rewriting them. ⇒ the leg that carries meaning is **where they are**: 2 inside `foldHalfStatuses`, 0 inside `main`. A **3** means someone re-inlined a fold; a **0 or 1** means the 「error outranks fail」 ordering objectui#5490 established was rewritten.

⭐ **Why the census needs both a hash and a count.** The count alone misses a **swapped** status (`error`→`fail` keeps 21). The hash alone misses a whole half deleted and another duplicated if the multiset happened to survive. ⚠️ And this census is the fix's own non-vacuity floor: `RECOGNISED_HALF_STATUSES` claims to be exactly the set the file declares, so if the file's literals move and the frozen list does not, the new test 「recognises exactly the statuses this file declares, re-derived from its source」 is what reds.

⚠️ The case floor is **138**, ⛔ not 127+11: the 127 was itself a runner reading, and I got the base wrong once already by counting `it(` call sites (107) and calling them tests.
